articles.title: 60 years after MLK protested in Marquette Park, marchers carry on his legacy
articles.description:
Bernice King looked out into the crowd of rain ponchos and umbrellas Saturday morning, echoing the calls of her father, who stood in the same spot 60 years before.

The Rev. Martin Luther King Jr. and other activists marched to Marquette Park in August 1966 to protest redlining and housing discrimination that spread in Chicago in the decades after droves of Black people moved north and settled in the city during the Great Migration. In Marquette Park that day, King and his associates were met with mobs of angry white people hurling rocks and Molotov cocktails.

This year, Bernice King joined Mayor Brandon Johnson, Chicago-born rapper Common and hundreds of marchers to commemorate the 60th anniversary of the march, reiterating that the fight for racial justice continues decades later.

Bernice King reminded the crowd of what her dad had dubbed the “triple evils” of poverty, racism and militarism.

“[Those] are still alive, still mutating, still menacing our communities,” she said. “They hide under new disguises, they show up in policies that punish the poor and systems that surveil the vulnerable, in structures that sacrifice humanity for profit.”

Hundreds of marchers braved the drizzly morning, congregating at 63rd Street and Kedzie Boulevard before making their way south to the park to the tune of protest songs, chants and upbeat horns and drums. Some wore shirts reading “Sixty years later, we’re still marching,” while listening to speakers hype up the crowd with stories of Black resilience and calls to action.

Common performed with singer Mumu Fresh and a group of backup singers, bringing a gospel tone to the gathering as people cheered and raised their fists in the crowd.

In her remarks, Bernice King spoke of being a toddler when her family lived in Chicago in the 1960s, begging her parents to let her march with them. She addressed the crowd and implored them to keep addressing injustices, calling out President Donald Trump's administration and federal immigration enforcement for heightened arrests and deportations, police brutality against people of color and voter suppression.

“We’re living in a time when human dignity is being dismissed, when truth is being twisted, when authoritarianism is out of control, when democracy is being deliberately undermined,” she said. “And yet in the midst of this trembling, we stand on the ground where my father once stood.”

Wearing a pink blazer embroidered with the words “Impact Over Fame,” she also stressed the strategy of nonviolence in fighting against oppression, saying it is the “discipline that keeps us from becoming what we oppose.”

Johnson said Chicago still faces many of the challenges it did in the 1960s when it comes to fair access to healthcare, housing, transportation, education and well-paying jobs, and said the “ultra-rich” need to be taxed to fund more public programs. He also spoke of his administration’s moves to increase affordable housing, add youth jobs and protect education initiatives that have been under attack by the federal government, like the Chicago Public Schools’ Black Student Success Plan.

“We’re building Chicago and we’re building a nation in a democracy that belongs to everyone,” Johnson said.

articles.title: Strategist floats bombshell theory for MAGA senator's silence on daughter's alleged abuser
articles.description: Critics have increasingly questioned the silence of Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-OH) regarding reports that his daughter, Emily Moreno, was allegedly abused by her husband, Rep. Max Miller (R-OH), but on Friday, a Democratic strategist said they believe they've figured out why. “THIS is why Bernie Moreno has been silent,” wrote Democratic strategist Ally Sammarco, founder of ARS Media, in a social media post Friday on X. “In March 2024, the AP reported that he used a work email to create a dating profile looking for gay sex. Max Miller has some dirt on him.” After reviewing a “massive and well-publicized data breach” of a “casual sexual encounters website” known as Adult Friend Finder, the Associated Press discovered an account created using Moreno’s email account with the username “nardo19672,” which the outlet noted “appears to refer to Moreno’s full first name, Bernardo, as well as the year and month of his birth in February 1967.” The user indicated they were seeking “Men for 1-on-1 sex.” Moreno has exhibited animosity toward the LGBTQ community, accusing LGBTQ advocates of pushing "radical" agendas of “indoctrination,” a radical shift from his previously seemingly pro-LGBTQ positions that began with his first bid for Senate in 2021. Miller, Moreno’s ex-son-in-law, has been accused of physically abusing his ex-wife, Moreno’s daughter. Miller was alleged to have beaten her, held a gun to her head and thrown boiling water on her, claims Miller has previously denied . Recent reporting has also revealed that Miller had “implicitly threatened” Moreno, Mother Jones reported , via an alleged text message uncovered in court records. “Take this however you want, everyone is going to get to know you better than your wife does,” Miller allegedly wrote to Moreno, according to Mother Jones. “Enjoy the ride brother, I wouldn’t have to do this if you could keep your lying daughter under control.” Moreno’s alleged profile on Adult Friend Finder, coupled with Miller’s alleged threats toward his ex-father-in-law, led a number of notable figures to concur with Sammarco’s theory. “No wonder Republicans do nothing with total control of the federal government!” wrote Grant Stern, executive editor of Occupy Democrats, in a social media post on X. “They're too busy extorting, wife beating, and cheating.” Martina Navratilova, a professional tennis icon, argued that Sammarco’s theory “explains a lot.” “Seems there is a lot of closeted gay men in the GOP – shame on their hypocrisy,” she wrote . Democratic strategist Mike Nellis largely expressed confusion over Moreno’s silence regarding the alleged abuse of his own daughter. “I don't understand Bernie Moreno at all,” Nellis wrote . “If you harmed a hair on my kid's head, I would crawl through broken glass to beat your a-- and care very little about the consequences. This guy can't even say that his daughter's attacker shouldn't run for reelection.” And Claude Taylor, a Democratic political activist and former White House staffer under the Clinton administration, took an especially sharp dig at Moreno, referencing his recent attack on Anthony Fauci. “Rather than disrespecting Dr Fauci, [Moreno] should respect that Anthony Fauci was a pioneer in the 1980 battle against AIDS,” Taylor wrote . “As a closeted gay man he should appreciate that fact.” THIS is why Bernie Moreno has been silent. articles.title: Republican slams Jeanine Pirro for passing the buck: 'Learned that from the top'
articles.description: Republicans lined up Saturday to hurl insults at former Fox News pundit Jeanine Pirro. Trump was first — taking to Truth Social to assert he "100%" disagreed with Pirro — then a onetime staffer of former House Speaker John Boehner (R-OH) and former Rep. Adam Kinzinger (R-IL) joined the queue. "I don't see her feeling as though she has to face any real repercussions," Maura Gillespie said on MS NOW Saturday morning. "If she can offload the blame to somebody else, she will." Pirro drew ire from Trump and Gillespie for very different reasons but on the same subject: her decision to drop charges against an Olympian canoeist on Friday. The U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia finally admitted to a lack of evidence that David Hearn, 67, vandalized the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. "Given all of this newly discovered information, it is difficult to attribute the widespread damage to the Reflecting Pool to vandalism, let alone to establish that fact beyond a reasonable doubt," Pirro said in a filing. While Trump raged at Pirro for rejecting his claim that vandalism — and not slapdash construction — was to blame for issues with the reflection pool lining, Gillespie unloaded on Pirro for trying to dodge blame. "P irro largely blamed the Department of Interior for the confusion on her part," Gillespie said. "[Pirro] learned that from the top." MS NOW host Alex Witt marveled at Pirro's sudden backtrack after having initially pursued the case with such aggression. In recent weeks, Pirro threatened a journalist and boasted of " tremendous evidence " as she defended the case. "She really came hard at this," said Witt. " That is her style, no doubt." Gillespie agreed, then took aim at the Trump administration for having botched the renovation job in the first place. "W hat's important to highlight is the misuse of funds," she said. " American dollars...are being spent frivolously because they're not being thoughtfully planned and orchestrated and decided upon. "If I were a Republican running for office right now, I would point to getting a better handle on our economy, getting a better handle on how our dollars are spent, which was the initial goal of the Trump administration."
